question: What is another name for compact bone tissue?
explanation: Compact bone is also called cortical bone because it forms the hard outer cortex of bones. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h1)

question: Where is compact bone tissue found in the highest amounts?

options.A: Inside the ends of short bones
options.B: Surrounding the bone marrow cavity loosely
options.C: In the shafts of long bones
options.D: Within the center of flat skull bones

explanation: The shafts of long bones need thick compact bone to bear body weight and resist bending forces. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the basic structural unit of compact bone tissue?
explanation: The osteon, or Haversian system, is the cylindrical functional unit that makes up the bulk of compact bone. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of tiny channels called canaliculi in compact bone?

options.A: To house the main blood vessels running down the bone
options.B: To anchor skeletal muscles securely to the bone surface
options.C: To connect bone cells so they can share food and waste
options.D: To produce new red blood cells in the bone marrow

explanation: Well done! Because the bone matrix is hard and blocks direct blood flow, these tiny channels (canaliculi) act like little highways letting bone cells pass nutrients back and forth. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which bone cell type is responsible for building new bone matrix?
explanation: Osteoblasts are the primary cells that build up and form new bone tissue. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h3)

question: What happens when an osteoblast gets completely trapped inside the hard bone it built?

options.A: It divides rapidly to form new osteons
options.B: It transforms back into a stem cell
options.C: It dissolves into the central canal
options.D: It turns into a mature osteocyte

explanation: Spot on! Once it's completely surrounded by the hard matrix, the builder cell settles down into a maintenance worker known as an osteocyte. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which mineral salt makes up the hard inorganic part of bone matrix?
explanation: Calcium phosphate crystals combine with other minerals to form hydroxyapatite, giving bone its hard, rigid quality. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is another name for the channels that run across compact bone to supply blood?
explanation: Great! Volkmann's canals run across (perpendicular to) the bone shaft, bringing blood vessels from the outside surface into the inner bone structure. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h5)

question: How do Volkmann's canals differ in direction from Haversian canals?

options.A: Volkmann's run horizontally, while Haversian run vertically
options.B: Volkmann's are microscopic, while Haversian are visible to the eye
options.C: Volkmann's are found in spongy bone, while Haversian are in compact bone
options.D: Volkmann's carry nerves only, while Haversian carry blood only

explanation: Spot on! Volkmann's run across horizontally, linking up nicely with the vertical central (Haversian) canals inside the osteons. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which structural feature is found in spongy bone instead of compact bone?
explanation: Spongy bone is made of a porous network of struts and plates called trabeculae, lacking standard osteon cylinders. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of compact bone when compared to spongy bone?

options.A: It forms the dense and solid outer layer of bones
options.B: It contains an organized system of osteons
options.C: It has a high concentration of red bone marrow inside it
options.D: It provides major structural support for body weight

explanation: Red bone marrow is primarily housed within the open spaces of spongy bone, not inside dense compact bone. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h6)

question: Besides providing support and protection, what mineral does compact bone primarily store?
explanation: Bone tissue stores large amounts of calcium and phosphorus, regulating mineral balance throughout the entire body. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h7)

question: How does compact bone contribute to movement?

options.A: By transmitting nerve impulses directly to muscle cells
options.B: By producing lubricating fluid for smooth joint movement
options.C: By acting as rigid levers that skeletal muscles pull against
options.D: By contracting actively alongside surrounding muscle fibers

explanation: Bones act as hard levers, allowing skeletal muscles to create coordinated body movement across joints. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h7)
